children: The Pentagon is deploying up to 10K additional troops and a third aircraft-carrier strike group to the Middle East, according to a media report published Thursday, as U.S. President Donald Trump
renewed military action against Iran following the midterm elections.

The newly dispatched naval forces, which include the aircraft carrier USS Theodore Roosevelt and the USS Makin Island Amphibious Ready Group, departed from San Diego this week and are scheduled to arrive by late November, the
This influx of fighter jets, warships and personnel from the 13th Marine Expeditionary Unit will bolster the more than 50K U.S. service members currently stationed in the region.

If the USS George Washington stays in the area upon the Roosevelt's arrival, it will join the USS George H.W. Bush to mark the first time three U.S. carrier strike groups have operated simultaneously in the Middle East since April, the
noted. These forces join the USS Boxer Amphibious Ready Group in waters that have seen sporadic combat since a fragile, temporary ceasefire collapsed earlier this year.

The significant troop buildup coincides with the Trump administration's recent rejection of a seven-day truce proposed by Tehran. Under the dismissed terms, Iran offered to reopen the economically vital Strait of Hormuz to global oil traffic and restart nuclear negotiations on the condition that the United States lift its ongoing blockade of Iranian seaports.
